  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Keshab Chandra Sen join the Brahmo Samaj?
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen joined the Brahmo Samaj in 1857, bringing new energy and youthful enthusiasm to the reform movement initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: Who appointed Keshab Chandra Sen as the 'Acharya' of the Brahmo Samaj?
practiceQuestions.sol: Debendranath Tagore appointed Keshab Chandra Sen as the Acharya of the Brahmo Samaj in 1862, recognizing his oratorical skills and deep dedication. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which breakaway faction of the Brahmo Samaj was established by Keshab Chandra Sen in 1866?
practiceQuestions.sol: Due to ideological differences with Debendranath Tagore, Keshab Chandra Sen and his followers broke away to form the 'Brahmo Samaj of India' in 1866, while Tagore's group became known as the Adi Brahmo Samaj. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Native Marriage Act (also known as the Civil Marriage Act) of 1872 was enacted largely due to the efforts of whom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen campaigned vigorously for social reform, leading to the enactment of the Native Marriage Act (1872), which prohibited child marriage and legalized inter-caste marriages. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which reformist organization was inspired by Keshab Chandra Sen's visit to Bombay in 1864?
opts: Both Prarthana Samaj and its ideological roots
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen's visit to Bombay in 1864 inspired local reformers like M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar to establish the Prarthana Samaj in 1867. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the new religious order founded by Keshab Chandra Sen in 1880, aiming to synthesize all world religions?
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1880, Keshab Chandra Sen proclaimed the 'Navavidhan' (New Dispensation), a universal religion uniting the truths of all major world religions. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Modern Indian History Texts]

practiceQuestions.q: The controversial marriage of Keshab Chandra Sen's underage daughter led to a major split in which organization?
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1878, Keshab Chandra Sen arranged the marriage of his 13-year-old daughter to the minor Maharaja of Cooch Behar, violating his own stance against child marriage and causing a split resulting in the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which prominent mystic and saint of Dakshineswar did Keshab Chandra Sen frequently visit and introduce to the urban elite of Calcutta?
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen was deeply influenced by Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and wrote extensively about him in his journals, popularizing Ramakrishna's teachings among Calcutta's educated middle class. [Primary Reference: Cultural Heritage of India / Modern History Texts]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the name of the journal edited by Keshab Chandra Sen to propagate Brahmo ideals?
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen helped establish and edit the 'Indian Mirror', a prominent newspaper that served as an organ for the Brahmo Samaj of India and voiced nationalist and reformist views. [Primary Reference: History of Indian Journalism / Modern History Compendium]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Keshab Chandra Sen visit England, delivering lecture tours that captivated British intellectuals?
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen visited Britain in 1870, where he met Queen Victoria and delivered powerful lectures on Indian social and spiritual reform, bridging East and West. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Keshab Chandra Sen’s approach to Brahmoism differ significantly from that of Debendranath Tagore's Adi Brahmo Samaj?
opts: Sen favored a rigidly orthodox Hindu revivalist framework, while Tagore was secular.
Sen championed radical social reforms and universalism, moving beyond Hindu scriptures, whereas Tagore remained tied to Hindu foundational texts and traditions.
Sen rejected monotheism entirely, while Tagore practiced rigorous monotheism.
Sen opposed women's education, whereas Tagore promoted it exclusively.
practiceQuestions.sol: Keshab Chandra Sen injected a more radical, cosmopolitan, and universalist vision into the Brahmo Samaj, incorporating elements from Christianity and other faiths, which clashed with Debendranath Tagore's more traditionalist and Hindu-scripture-bound approach. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the underlying philosophical objective behind Keshab Chandra Sen's formulation of 'Navavidhan' (New Dispensation)?
opts: To convert all of India exclusively to Christianity
To synthesize the eternal truths of all world religions into a universal spiritual harmony
To establish a political party aimed at overthrowing British rule
To revive Vedic rituals and animal sacrifices
practiceQuestions.sol: Navavidhan represented Sen's mature philosophical synthesis, asserting that God had progressively revealed truth through various prophets and religions across the world, creating a harmony of all faiths. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian Social Thought Compendium]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Keshab Chandra Sen's perspective on British rule in India evolve during his lifetime?
opts: He started as a violent revolutionary and ended up as a British spy.
Initially, he viewed British rule as a divine providence that would bring modernization and moral elevation, though he later critiqued colonial exploitation and administrative high-handedness.
He consistently called for an immediate armed rebellion against the British Crown.
He was entirely indifferent to politics and focused only on esoteric mysticism.
practiceQuestions.sol: Like many 19th-century Indian intellectuals, Sen initially saw British rule through the lens of 'Providence'—believing it would introduce Western science, liberty, and social reform—while retaining a critical eye on racial arrogance. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: What systemic impact did the 1878 Brahmo schism (over the Cooch Behar marriage) have on the broader Indian socio-religious reform movement?
opts: It ended all reform activities across India permanently.
It demonstrated the internal ideological tensions between charismatic leadership and democratic institutionalization, leading to more secular and democratic structures like the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.
It merged the Brahmo Samaj completely with the orthodox Hindu Mahasabha.
It forced the British government to ban all religious societies.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 1878 split highlighted the danger of authoritarian tendencies under a charismatic leader (Sen), prompting younger radicals like Ananda Mohan Bose and Sivasathnath Sastri to establish the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj on strictly democratic and constitutional principles. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Keshab Chandra Sen utilize print media and public lectures as instruments of social engineering?
opts: He used them exclusively for secret political conspiracies against the British.
He harnessed English and vernacular press alongside emotive, persuasive public speeches to mobilize public opinion against caste rigidities and child marriage.
He avoided public speaking entirely and relied solely on manuscripts.
He published materials only in Sanskrit to maintain elitist exclusivity.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen was a master orator and journalist who recognized that modernization required active public discourse. Through journals like 'Indian Mirror' and stirring lectures across India and Britain, he galvanized reformist consciousness. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Modern Indian Press History]

practiceQuestions.q: In what ways did Keshab Chandra Sen's reform agenda address the 'women's question' in 19th-century India?
opts: By advocating for strict adherence to purdah and confinement within the household
By promoting female education, campaigning against child marriage, supporting widow remarriage, and encouraging women's public participation
By opposing female suffrage and property rights
By limiting women's roles strictly to religious domestic rituals
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen placed women's emancipation at the core of his social reform program, advocating for female education, raising the age of marriage, and providing women a more active role in Samaj activities, though paradoxically his own actions regarding his daughter's marriage caused a severe crisis. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of Keshab Chandra Sen's interaction with diverse religious traditions (Hinduism, Christianity, Islam, Buddhism)?
opts: It caused him to abandon spirituality altogether in favor of strict materialism.
It laid the intellectual groundwork for Indian secularism and comparative religion by promoting ecumenism and mutual respect among faiths.
It resulted in the creation of a militant religious militia.
It isolated India from global philosophical discourse.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen's comparative study of religions and his synthesis of Christian ethics with Hindu spiritual philosophy pioneered a universalist approach that deeply influenced modern Indian pluralism and inter-faith dialogue. [Primary Reference: Cultural Heritage of India / Modern Indian Philosophy]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the ideological trajectory of the Brahmo Samaj under Keshab Chandra Sen affect provincial reform movements outside Bengal?
opts: It had zero influence outside Bengal due to language barriers.
His tours and ideas served as a catalytic template, inspiring reformers in Bombay, Madras, and Northern India to establish parallel indigenous reform bodies like Prarthana Samaj.
It caused violent anti-Bengal riots across western India.
It forced regional reformers to adopt orthodox caste practices.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen's extensive travel across India catalyzed the spread of reformist ideas, directly leading to the founding of the Prarthana Samaj in Maharashtra and encouraging similar monotheistic and social reform groups in other regions. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: What criticism did Keshab Chandra Sen face from orthodox Hindus as well as radical Brahmo reformers?
opts: Orthodox Hindus criticized him for westernized syncretism and breaking caste norms, while radical Brahmos accused him of autocratic tendencies and ritualistic deviations (such as the Cooch Behar marriage).
Both groups criticized him for being too communist and anti-property.
Both groups praised him universally with no criticism whatsoever.
He was criticized solely for supporting the 1857 Revolt.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen occupied a complex middle ground: traditionalists rejected his social radicalism and borrowing from Christianity, while young Brahmo reformers grew disillusioned with his personal authoritarianism and compromises on social laws. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra - India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Keshab Chandra Sen's engagement with Christian thought influence his interpretation of Bhakti and devotion?
opts: He completely replaced Hindu Bhakti with European secularism.
He integrated Christian concepts of personal God, fatherhood of God, and self-surrender with traditional Vaishnava Bhakti, creating a passionate, devotional emotionalism in Brahmo worship.
He rejected all forms of emotional devotion in favor of strict atheistic rationalism.
He advocated for mandatory baptism into the Church of England for all members.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sen deeply admired Jesus Christ (publishing lectures like 'Jesus Christ: Europe and Asia') and blended Christian devotional ethics with Hindu Bhakti, infusing the Brahmo movement with a vibrant, emotional spiritualism. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian Religious History Compendium]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Keshab Chandra Sen:
1. He was appointed as the Acharya of the Brahmo Samaj by Debendranath Tagore in 1862.
2. He founded the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866 after parting ways with Debendranath Tagore.
3. He strongly opposed the enactment of the Native Marriage Act of 1872.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Sen was made Acharya in 1862 and formed the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866. Statement 3 is incorrect because Sen actively campaigned for and supported the Native Marriage Act (1872) to ban child marriage, rather than opposing it. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the split of the Brahmo Samaj in 1878:
1. The split was triggered by Keshab Chandra Sen arranging the marriage of his underage daughter against Brahmo principles.
2. The breakaway faction formed by the dissenters was called the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. In 1878, Sen's underage daughter's marriage to the Cooch Behar ruler caused outrage among progressive members, leading to a split and the formation of the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj by leaders like Ananda Mohan Bose and Sivasathnath Sastri. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Keshab Chandra Sen's international and religious outlook:
1. He visited Britain in 1870 and interacted with British social reformers and Queen Victoria.
2. He founded the 'Navavidhan' (New Dispensation) to propagate an exclusive sectarian form of Christianity in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sen visited Britain in 1870, addressing large audiences and meeting Queen Victoria. Statement 2 is incorrect because 'Navavidhan' was not an exclusive Christian sect, but rather a universalist religious synthesis encompassing the truths of all world religions. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History Compendium]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Keshab Chandra Sen's association with Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa:
1. Keshab Chandra Sen frequently met Ramakrishna at Dakshineswar and publicized his spiritual wisdom in Brahmo journals like 'Indian Mirror'.
2. This interaction helped introduce Ramakrishna's teachings to the English-educated urban intelligentsia of Calcutta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sen's deep appreciation for Ramakrishna bridged the gap between the westernized Brahmo elite and traditional Indian mysticism, bringing Ramakrishna into wider public prominence. [Primary Reference: Cultural Heritage of India / Modern History Texts]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the impact of Keshab Chandra Sen on regional social reform:
1. His 1864 visit to Madras and Bombay directly inspired the formation of the Prarthana Samaj.
2. He advocated for the abolition of the caste system and supported inter-caste marriages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sen's extensive tours galvanized reformers across India. He consistently critiqued caste rigidities and promoted inter-caste marriages, which formed a legislative cornerstone in the Native Marriage Act (1872). [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Keshab Chandra Sen's journalistic ventures:
1. He was associated with the editing and management of the newspaper 'Indian Mirror'.
2. Through his publications, he strictly propagated orthodox Hindu rituals and opposed modern scientific education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sen was a driving force behind the 'Indian Mirror', the first Indian daily newspaper in English. Statement 2 is incorrect because Sen championed modern science, social reform, and rationalism, actively opposing orthodox rituals and caste barriers. [Primary Reference: History of Indian Journalism / Modern History Compendium]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the ideological differences between Debendranath Tagore and Keshab Chandra Sen:
1. Debendranath Tagore wanted the Brahmo Samaj to retain close ties with Hindu scriptures and traditions, whereas Keshab Chandra Sen favored a more universalist approach incorporating Western and Christian ethics.
2. Both men agreed completely on the abolition of caste distinctions and the adoption of radical social legislation without compromise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Tagore represented a more Hindu-centric reformism, while Sen introduced universalist and cosmopolitan elements. Statement 2 is incorrect because Tagore was more cautious regarding rapid social changes and inter-caste marriages compared to the radical approach initially championed by Sen. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Keshab Chandra Sen's views on women's education and emancipation:
1. He established institutions and advocated for women's education and the suppression of child marriage.
2. He believed that women should remain confined to domestic religious duties and should not participate in public lectures or Samaj administration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sen was a pioneer in advocating for female education and fighting child marriage. Statement 2 is incorrect because Sen actively encouraged women to step out of purdah, attend Samaj meetings, and participate in reform work (even though his views on gender roles had some 19th-century patriarchal limitations). [Primary Reference: Modern Indian Social History Texts]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural legacy of Keshab Chandra Sen's movement:
1. The Brahmo Samaj under Sen suffered from organizational splits due to autocratic control and controversies over ritualistic practices.
2. Despite internal fractures, Sen's movement played a pivotal role in shaping modern Indian legislative reforms on marriage and civil rights.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Sen's leadership style provoked splits (1866 and 1878), yet his energetic campaigns directly yielded landmark legislation such as the Native Marriage Act of 1872, shaping the trajectory of modern social reform in India. [Primary Reference: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Keshab Chandra Sen's philosophical evolution in his later years:
1. He proclaimed the 'Navavidhan' or New Dispensation, emphasizing the harmony of all religions under a unified divine guidance.
2. He rejected the concept of God entirely and declared himself an agnostic rationalist.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: In 1880, Sen announced the Navavidhan, symbolizing his synthesis of world religions. Statement 2 is incorrect because Sen remained deeply spiritual and religious throughout his life, never adopting atheism or agnosticism. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian Religious Philosophy Compendium]
